# Device cost comparison: $/GB of every device/material concept vs DDR5

**Generated by:** `models/device_cost_compare.py` (agent `p3-devmodel`) · **As of:** 2026-11-01 · **Inputs:** `research/phase2/A1|A2|A3_device_params.json`, `tmp_to_id.json`, `concepts_master.json`, `research/phase1/cost_inputs.json`, DDR5 reference from `models/dram_cost_stack.py` (`ddr5_reference()`) · **Re-run:** `python3 models/device_cost_compare.py` · **Assumptions:** `research/assumptions/p3-devmodel.md`

All values are [ESTIMATE] unless a row's source column gives a URL. Ranges come from the sensitivity table.

```text
DEVICE COST COMPARISON  --  $/GB of every device/material concept vs DDR5   (agent p3-devmodel, as of 2026-11-01)
DDR5 reference: import models/dram_cost_stack.py: ddr5_reference()
  DDR5 16Gb 1b incumbent COST     $1.484/GB   (raw GB, packaged component)
  DDR5 Q4-2026 contract PRICE     $20.367/GB
  DDR5 A-05 glut PRICE (-60%)     $8.147/GB
  DDR5 severe glut PRICE          $2.037/GB
Formula: $/GB = wafer_cost / (usable_mm2 x density_Gb/mm2 / 8 x yield) + test_pkg_$/GB
         density = 1e6/cell_um2 x array_eff x bits/cell x layers / 1e9 (filed die density wins; eff back-solved)
         usable_mm2 = GDPW(100 mm2 die) x 100: 300mm 60334 mm2 (0.854 of wafer), 200mm 24817 mm2 (0.790)
Sensitivity: wafer cost x0.7 / x1.3; yield 0.95 / 0.50; best = (x0.7, 0.95), worst = (x1.3, 0.50)

Flags: DENS=filed die density from filing (eff_used back-solved) | DENS=cell from cell area | DENS=default claim-parity default
       MISMATCH filed density >10% off the cell formula (A2 uses binary Gb; XPoint measured die vs cell) | EMB embedded/buyer row, test+pkg=0 as filed
       CLAIM company/marketing claim | HYP hypothetical line | UNSUP Rule-1 UNSUPPORTED concept | ACQ acquisition $/GB, yield = test pass rate
       SHEET Gen-8.5 glass sheet | DIRECT $/GB from label cost | W/Y/TP=default documented default | DCS dram_cost_stack case
Defaults used when a filing lacks a value:
  ref_die_mm2            100.0    ESTIMATE: reference die for wafer utilisation (A3 convention: 100 mm2 die, ~85% usable)
  array_efficiency       0.5      ESTIMATE: midpoint of filed array efficiencies (0.30-0.70)
  bits_per_cell          1        ESTIMATE: single-level cell unless filed
  layers                 1        ESTIMATE: planar unless filed
  yield_lab              0.3      ESTIMATE: TRL 2-3 lab process with no production line
  tp_usd_per_mm2         0.015    ESTIMATE: A3 convention, test+package $1.50 per 100 mm2 die => $/GB = 0.12/density
  sheet_utilisation      0.9      ESTIMATE: usable fraction of a Gen-8.5 glass sheet
  claim_parity_density   0.3902   ESTIMATE: no density filed; assume the claim (DRAM-like $/GB) means DDR5 1b density (16Gb / 41 mm2, dram_cost_stack)
  wafer_2d_adder         1000.0   ESTIMATE: 2D-material tier (transfer or low-T growth, +4-6 masks) on a 200mm 130nm wafer
  optane_acq_usd_per_gb  1.4      ESTIMATE: midpoint of A2's [UNVERIFIED] $0.8-2/GB ITAD acquisition range
  label_usd              0.1      ESTIMATE: A3 filing, ~$0.10 per printed 20-bit label
  label_bits             20       ESTIMATE: A3 filing, 20-bit label
  yield_ref_sram         0.9      ESTIMATE: mature logic die yield for SRAM reference rows
```

## Interpretation (p3-devmodel, 2026-11-01)

1. **Headline.** 44 concept ids are costed: 41 from branch-A device rows, plus C-58, C-59 and C-71 from the DRAM model or their cards. 8 get under the A-05 glut price ($8.15/GB) at base inputs: C-05, C-08, C-11, C-15, C-25, C-26, C-58, C-59. Only C-05, C-25 reach DDR5 incumbent cost ($1.48/GB) in the best case (at base inputs: C-05, C-25). Every sub-glut concept has a catch: C-05 at $1.22/GB rests on NEO's unverified ~10x density claim with single-cell proof of concept only; C-08 at $4.19/GB was never productized by Micron and needs a DRAM fab; C-11 at $5.08/GB is Rule-1 UNSUPPORTED, and its density is a claim-parity default; C-15 at $2.94/GB is Samsung's device (the venture sells IGZO targets and precursors, so this cost is a demand signal, not venture revenue); C-25 at $0.99/GB needs a T4 crosspoint fab and died on volume and ecosystem, not cost (A2 notes); C-26 at $2.06/GB is a shrinking inventory of used modules with an UNVERIFIED acquisition price, usable only in Cascade/Ice Lake Xeons; C-58 at $3.28/GB needs a T4 fab ($2-3.5B) and would be the highest-cost producer against Micron 1-alpha; C-59 at $4.12/GB cannot get foundry wafers in a shortage and has no U.S. manufacturing.
2. **Die on $/GB alone (Rule 4, no other axis): C-03, C-30, C-35, C-38, C-42.** Even with wafer cost -30% and 0.95 yield, the best case stays above the glut price, and the cards name no other axis a buyer pays for. That covers display-glass IGZO (C-03, $291/GB), floating-body 1T-DRAM (C-30, best $15.6), bulk SRAM as a DRAM substitute (C-35, best $53.4 at the cheapest node) and wafer-scale SRAM (C-38, $1,007). C-42, printed polymer ($4.44e+07/GB), is also Rule-1 UNSUPPORTED.
3. **C-02, the standalone IGZO 2T0C die, is dead on $/GB as defined.** On a U.S. 200mm 130nm line it costs $360/GB (best $176). A1's hypothetical 300mm 28nm BEOL line, which no U.S. foundry offers, would cost $11.9/GB (best $6.86), below the $8.15 glut price only at the best-case corner. Its only axis is refresh power, and commodity DRAM buyers do not pay for that, so Rule 4 kills it. The IGZO value lives in the embedded and refresh-power cards (C-01, C-04).
4. **The DRAM-class challengers (C-04, C-08, C-09) beat the glut price only on DRAM-fab wafers at DRAM-like yields.** OCTRAM costs $8.50/GB (best $4.26), Micron NVDRAM $4.19 (best $2.41) and FMC DRAM+ $14.8 (best $6.39). None reaches the $1.48 incumbent cost, and in a severe glut ($2.04) all lose. They survive on non-volatility or refresh power, but each needs a DRAM fab with a capacitor module (T3/T4). This founder cannot build that, and no U.S. foundry offers one.
5. **MRAM survives only on non-$/GB axes (C-16, C-17, C-18, C-19, C-20, C-21, C-27, C-28, C-51).** Computed cost runs $71.7-3,797/GB, and the Everspin 1Gb street price ($821/GB) is 101x the glut price. Even a hypothetical 14nm 4Gb part costs $71.7/GB (best $42.3). So C-20, MRAM as main memory, is dead on $/GB. The rest live only on non-volatility, lifecycle, rad-hard or provenance, and they are sold per chip or per card, not per GB.
6. **Ferroelectric, ReRAM, CBRAM, CNT and AlScN memories (C-06, C-07, C-10, C-12, C-22, C-23, C-24, C-40) cost $30.7-5,021/GB**, 3.77x-616x the glut price. They are embedded or kilobit-to-megabit parts. Their business is non-volatility, rad-hard, 500-600C temperature (C-07), compute energy (C-24) or U.S. provenance, so score them on those axes. NRAM (C-40, best $18.1) gets closest, but only to the 2026 contract price.
7. **Bulk SRAM never drops below about $78.7/GB at any node.** The 2-65nm rows span $78.7-267/GB, with a best case of $53.4, so trailing nodes are not cheaper per bit. SRAM concepts C-33, C-35, C-36, C-37, C-38, C-39 can never win on $/GB. C-33 and C-36 survive on provenance and lifecycle, C-37 and C-39 on compute energy and latency, and C-35 and C-38 are dead.
8. **Gain-cell eDRAM (C-01, C-32, C-43) competes with SRAM, not DRAM.** The Si 2T/3T gain cell at 28nm costs $47.1/GB area-equivalent vs $87.3/GB for 6T SRAM on a 28nm wafer. The 130nm IGZO macro (C-01) costs $543/GB vs $1,585/GB for 130nm SkyWater SRAM. So the Rule-4 axis for these cards is on-die density and standby power vs SRAM, for edge-ASIC, defense and cryo buyers, not $/GB vs DDR5.
9. **Only-in-a-shortage concepts (tier C: C-30, C-31, C-40)** beat the $20.37 Q4-2026 contract price in their best case but never the glut price. T-RAM costs $17.7 (best $11.5), floating-body DRAM $23.8 (best $15.6) and NRAM $30.7 (best $18.1). Under Rule 6 they die in a 2028-29 glut unless a non-$/GB axis carries them. Out-of-branch check: a licensed legacy DDR4 fab (C-58) costs $3.28/GB in the canonical model and a PSMC-foundry DDR3 brand (C-59) $4.12/GB, both below the glut price. Their cards fail on capital and wafer allocation, not unit cost.
10. **Method caveats.** Branch-filed DRAM-class wafer costs ($5.5-7k) are 45-84% above the canonical $3,800 1b wafer, so the branches' own DDR5 references compute at $2.70-2.71/GB vs the model's $1.48. The -30% wafer case is therefore the fair comparison. Gb is decimal in A1/A3 and binary in A2 (up to 7.4% apart). Embedded rows carry no test or package cost, by filing. The live model deck (cost $1.48, contract $20.37, glut $8.15) differs from the brief's ($1.64 / $15.99 / $6.40); tier changes between the two: C-26 A->B, C-40 D->C. UNSUPPORTED concepts (C-11, C-41, C-42) die under Rule 1 whatever their $/GB, and C-11's sub-glut number rests only on a claim-parity default density.

Best case (wafer cost -30%, yield 0.95) is still at or above the A-05 glut price ($8.15/GB): C-01, C-02, C-03, C-06, C-07, C-10, C-12, C-16, C-17, C-18, C-19, C-20, C-21, C-22, C-23, C-24, C-27, C-28, C-30, C-31, C-32, C-33, C-34, C-35, C-36, C-37, C-38, C-39, C-40, C-41, C-42, C-43, C-51, C-71.

Not even below the Q4-2026 contract price ($20.37/GB) in the best case (tier D): C-01, C-02, C-03, C-06, C-07, C-10, C-12, C-16, C-17, C-18, C-19, C-20, C-21, C-22, C-23, C-24, C-27, C-28, C-32, C-33, C-34, C-35, C-36, C-37, C-38, C-39, C-41, C-42, C-43, C-51, C-71.

Robust to the deck choice (cannot win under either the live model deck or the task-brief deck): C-01, C-02, C-03, C-06, C-07, C-10, C-12, C-16, C-17, C-18, C-19, C-20, C-21, C-22, C-23, C-24, C-27, C-28, C-30, C-31, C-32, C-33, C-34, C-35, C-36, C-37, C-38, C-39, C-40, C-41, C-42, C-43, C-51, C-71.

Could win on $/GB, at least at the glut price (tiers A/B): C-04, C-05, C-08, C-09, C-11, C-15, C-25, C-26, C-58, C-59. None of them is a device this founder can build. C-11 is Rule-1 UNSUPPORTED and C-05 rests on a company claim. C-26 is salvage of used modules, and C-15 is a materials play riding Samsung's device. C-04, C-08, C-09, C-25 and C-58 need a DRAM- or crosspoint-class 300mm fab (T3/T4), and C-59 needs foundry DRAM wafers that are allocated away in a shortage.
